mission.title: Install and Configure Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS)
mission.description: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) is a managed Kubernetes service that simplifies the process of running Kubernetes on AWS. It is ideal for users who want to leverage AWS's infrastructure and services while maintaining control over their Kubernetes clusters. Key trade-offs include reliance on AWS services and potential costs associated with resource usage.

steps.title: Install the AWS CLI
steps.description:
The AWS CLI is required to interact with AWS services, including EKS. Ensure you have the latest version installed.

```bash

pip install awscli --upgrade --user

```

> Install or upgrade AWS CLI to the latest version.

steps.title: Create an EKS Cluster
steps.description:
This command creates an EKS cluster with the specified Kubernetes version, node count, and region.

```bash

aws eks create-cluster --name my-cluster --kubernetes-version 1.31 --role-arn arn:aws:iam::YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID:role/EKS-Cluster-Role --resources-vpc-config subnetIds=subnet-12345678,subnet-87654321 --region us-west-2

```

> Replace YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID with your actual AWS account ID.
commands: aws eks create-cluster --name my-cluster --kubernetes-version 1.31 --role-arn arn:aws:iam::YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID:role/EKS-Cluster-Role --resources-vpc-config subnetIds=subnet-12345678,subnet-87654321 --region us-west-2

steps.title: Update kubeconfig
steps.description:
This command updates your kubeconfig file to use the new EKS cluster, allowing kubectl to interact with it.

```bash

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name my-cluster --region us-west-2

```

> Ensure you are using the correct region.

steps.title: Verify Cluster Nodes
steps.description:
This command checks the status of the nodes in your EKS cluster to ensure they are running.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> You should see the nodes listed with a 'Ready' status.

steps.title: Post-Install Configuration
steps.description:
Set up monitoring and autoscaling for your cluster to ensure optimal performance.

```bash

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/master/cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/aws/examples/cluster-autoscaler-template.yaml

```

> This sets up the cluster autoscaler.

uninstall.title: Delete the EKS Cluster
uninstall.description:
This command will delete the EKS cluster and all associated resources, leading to potential data loss.

```bash

aws eks delete-cluster --name my-cluster --region us-west-2

```

> This will remove the cluster and all associated resources.

uninstall.title: Clean Up Orphaned Resources
uninstall.description:
After deleting the cluster, check for and manually delete any orphaned resources such as load balancers and PVCs.

```bash

aws ec2 describe-load-balancers --region us-west-2

```

> List load balancers to identify any that need to be deleted.

upgrade.title: Upgrade the EKS Cluster
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you back up your data and configurations. Then proceed with the upgrade.

```bash

aws eks update-cluster-version --name my-cluster --kubernetes-version 1.31 --region us-west-2

```

> This command upgrades the cluster to the specified version.

upgrade.title: Verify Upgrade Status
upgrade.description:
Check the status of the upgrade to ensure it completed successfully.

```bash

aws eks describe-cluster --name my-cluster --region us-west-2

```

> Look for the 'status' field to confirm the upgrade.

upgrade.title: Post-Upgrade Verification
upgrade.description:
Verify that all nodes are in a 'Ready' state after the upgrade.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> Ensure all nodes are listed with a 'Ready' status.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This error indicates that your kubeconfig is not set up correctly or the cluster is not reachable.

**Fix:**
Run 'aws eks update-kubeconfig --name my-cluster --region us-west-2' to update your kubeconfig.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'No resources found in kube-system namespace'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the necessary components are not deployed in the kube-system namespace.

**Fix:**
Check the cluster status and ensure that the EKS control plane is active.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Insufficient capacity in your availability zones'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This error occurs when there are not enough resources available in the specified AZs.

**Fix:**
Try creating the cluster in a different region or AZ with available capacity.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Failed to create cluster: Cluster creation failed'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This can happen due to misconfigured IAM roles or VPC settings.

**Fix:**
Verify that the IAM role has the necessary permissions and that the VPC configuration is correct.

versionNotes.changes: Added support for Kubernetes 1.31, improved integration with AWS services.
versionNotes.deprecations: Deprecated support for Kubernetes versions below 1.28.
versionNotes.migrationSteps: If upgrading from 1.30, ensure to review the new IAM permissions required for the latest features.

resolution.summary: You should see the output of 'kubectl get nodes' showing all nodes in 'Ready' state, confirming that your EKS cluster is operational.
